rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2013> two-season (2008<U+2013>2009) field experiment at E<U+011F>irdir Fruit Growing Research Station, Isparta, Turkey, comparing a flood-irrigated control with eight drip irrigation schedules (2 intervals x 4 pan coefficients) on Starkrimson Delicious apple, with ANOVA/Duncan tests on measured fruit quality and shoot growth.
rows.notes: The passage claims that studies on conversion from flood to drip irrigation assessed yield and all reported yield increases. This study does not measure or report yield (kg/tree or t/ha). It reports fruit quality (diameter, length, weight, flesh firmness, soluble solids, colour, commercial size-class ratios) and vegetative growth (shoot number, length, diameter), finding drip treatments generally gave larger fruit, higher extra/class 1 ratios and more shoot growth than flood irrigation; flood irrigation had lower soluble solids. Lower yield under drip is mentioned only as a grower complaint in the Introduction, not as a measured result. Because the claimed effect (yield increase) is not reported, Q2 is 'no' and Q3<U+2013>Q9 follow. For the record, the study is a single site/soil/crop (clay loam, one cultivar), plot scale, reports no dispersion statistics beyond Duncan letter groupings and regression significance, and states only a generic restriction that recommendations apply to 'similar climatic and soil conditions'.

notes: Document text lacks highlights, abstract, keywords, tables and figures (only captions referenced), and references, but the full body text (methods, results, discussion, conclusion) is present and sufficient to confirm that yield was not measured.
